query: I signed an unconditional contract at 6:30 pm AEST on 12 May 2026 to buy an established Melbourne apartment as an investment, and settlement occurred on 30 June 2026. In the 2027-28 income year I expect $35,000 in rent, $55,000 in otherwise deductible interest and property expenses, and a $140,000 salary. Can the $20,000 rental loss still reduce my salary income under current federal tax law? Please identify the event and time that control the transitional treatment rather than assuming the settlement date decides it.

I entered into a contract at 8:00 pm AEST on 12 May 2026 to buy an established Brisbane rental house and settled in July 2026. In 2027-28 the property produces $40,000 of rent and $70,000 of otherwise deductible expenses, while I earn a $110,000 salary. I may sell the house in 2030. Explain whether the $30,000 excess can offset my salary, how any amount that cannot be used is treated in later years or on sale, and whether I can simply add it to the property's CGT cost base.

I am considering signing in August 2026 for an off-the-plan apartment that will be completed in June 2027 and has never been occupied. I expect it to make a rental loss in 2027-28. Under the tax reforms now enacted, would the new-build exception preserve ordinary negative-gearing treatment, and what would I need to verify before relying on that exception? Please distinguish the Act itself from any definition or requirement that depends on a legislative instrument, and also flag the CGT choices that may matter if I later sell.

I am an Australian-resident individual who bought listed shares in 2023, will still own them on 30 June 2027, and expects to sell them in August 2028. My accountant proposes applying the old 50% CGT discount to the whole gain because I held the shares for more than 12 months. Analyse that advice under the law enacted in 2026, including the transitional deemed sale and reacquisition, treatment of the pre-1 July 2027 and later portions of the gain, post-commencement indexation, and the new minimum tax rate on relevant capital gains.

I will receive the age pension throughout 2028-29 and expect to sell a long-held investment asset that year. A friend says every Australian resident must now pay at least 30% tax on every capital gain realised after 1 July 2027. Is that right? Please separate how my gain is calculated from whether the minimum-rate rule and any exception apply.

I had a total superannuation balance of $2.9 million just before 1 July 2026 and $4.2 million at 30 June 2027, with positive relevant superannuation earnings during 2026-27. I have heard three conflicting claims: that Division 296 never became law, that it taxes all of my fund earnings at an extra flat 15%, and that the $3 million threshold is permanently unindexed. Explain the enacted regime that applies to me, when it first operates, the proportional approach to taxable superannuation earnings, how the thresholds are indexed, and whether there is now a separate treatment for balances above $10 million.

I run an Australian business with 22 employees and pay wages weekly. For the payday on 3 July 2026, payroll calculated super using our old ordinary-time-earnings settings and assumed we could keep paying contributions quarterly through the Small Business Superannuation Clearing House. What changed from 1 July 2026? Give me a practical compliance analysis covering qualifying earnings, the contribution rate, when the fund must receive a payment, any relevant transition or extended timeframes, the consequences of a shortfall, and the clearing-house closure.

My corporate group has annual Australian revenue of $560 million and plans to acquire 100% of an Australian software company with annual Australian revenue of $14 million in October 2026. The board believes Australian merger review is still voluntary and wants to complete first after requesting informal ACCC clearance. Under the current regime, assess whether notification is mandatory, whether we must wait before completing, what thresholds and exemptions need to be checked, and whether a notification waiver could change the position.

I am a solicitor in Sydney. In July 2026 an overseas client asks my firm to establish an Australian company, manage money through our trust account, create a family trust, and handle the purchase of a warehouse. I have always understood that lawyers are outside the federal AML/CTF regime and that legal professional privilege prevents any reporting. Under the law now in force, which of these services may bring the firm into the regime, what enrolment, risk-assessment, customer-due-diligence and reporting steps should I consider, and how does privilege actually interact with those obligations?

In June 2026 my neighbour deliberately pointed a hidden camera into my bathroom and uploaded the footage to a private online group. Neither of us is covered by the Australian Privacy Principles. Can I now bring a federal claim for serious invasion of privacy? Explain the elements, public-interest test, defences, time limit, remedies, and whether the OAIC handles the claim.

I separated from my spouse in May 2025 and filed a federal property proceeding in July 2025. During the marriage my spouse controlled all bank access, incurred debts in my name, and threatened the family dog when I tried to leave. My spouse now proposes that we share ownership and alternate care of the dog after separation. Explain how the family-property laws applying to my proceeding deal with the economic effect of family violence, liabilities and wastage, the duty of financial disclosure, and the orders a court can and cannot make about a companion animal.

My Australian company had $4.2 million turnover in the previous financial year. In June 2026 a ransomware attacker stole customer data, and our cyber insurer paid the attacker on our behalf; I learned of the payment the next day. Management says reporting the payment is voluntary because the insurer paid it and no critical-infrastructure asset was affected. Is that correct? Give me an urgent action plan addressing the current ransomware-payment reporting duty and deadline, who must report, what information is required, and how that duty differs from any privacy or critical-infrastructure incident notification.

My mother entered a government-funded aged care home in December 2025. The provider restricts family visits, refuses to recognise her chosen supporter, and reduced activities after she complained. Staff rely on the old Charter of Aged Care Rights. What rights and complaint protections apply now, and what should we do?

My child was born on 2 July 2026, but I lodged a pre-birth Parental Leave Pay claim in June. I have a partner. How many payment days do we now have, how many are reserved for my partner, and will my earlier claim be updated? Also explain the super contribution, including its rate, who pays it, and when.

I own a restaurant company with 40 employees. Since February 2025, the finance director has deliberately removed recorded overtime before each payroll run to cut labour costs, and I discovered the practice in January 2026. The director says deliberate wage underpayment is still only a civil Fair Work issue. Assess the company's and individuals' possible criminal and civil exposure under the current law, the importance of intent and the dates of the conduct, and the roles of the Fair Work Ombudsman, cooperation agreements and criminal prosecutors.

I operate an online service available in Australia that lets logged-in users create profiles, post videos, follow one another and receive a personalised recommendation feed. In March 2026 we began allowing children under 16 to keep accounts if a parent consents. I thought Australia's social-media age law penalised children and parents rather than platforms, and that parental consent solved the issue. Analyse whether the current minimum-age obligation is likely to cover the service, what reasonable-steps duty and civil exposure may apply, and whether the March 2026 rules or exclusions affect the assessment.
